summary: Two levers carried almost all of the -0.019 from the 0.997333 baseline: batch size and attention window length. Halving the batch to 2**18 (grad_accum 2->1, LRs untouched) alone was -0.0088 and replicated four times; capacity then wanted more width (dim 512->640->768 at depth 8) and much shorter sliding windows (S layers seq/2 -> seq/4 -> seq/8, which is far more than the 5-7% extra tokens from cheaper attention can explain). My final config stacks width 768 with window seq/8 at depth 8 / MLP 4x / batch 2**18 / WARMDOWN 0.7: val_bpb 0.978436, 65.5GB. What did not work: batch 2**17 either at fixed LR (0.9948-0.9961) or with all LRs halved to match the total update distance (0.989610) -- so 2**18 is a genuine optimum, not an LR artefact; HEAD_DIM 128->64 at fixed width was badly worse (0.993673); and the depth-10/MLP-3x reshape that helped at width 512 hurt at width 640. Next I would push the window direction to its turnover (seq/16, and a pattern with only one full-attention layer), then re-probe width 896 with a chunked loss head now that attention is cheap, and only then revisit the LR schedule, which is flat to within ~5e-4 near the optimum.
